subject: computer-science
title: Higher-Order Functions and Recursion
welcome_lead: Functions that take and return functions — plus recursion patterns.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: map, filter, fold/reduce and recursion as iteration.
final_note: Higher-order tools replace many for-loops with one line.

concepts.def: A function that takes or returns another function.
Apply a function to every element of a list, returning a new list.
Keep elements of a list that satisfy a predicate.
Combine list elements into a single value with a binary function (also reduce).
A function that calls itself, reducing toward a base case.
A recursive call as the last action — can be optimised to a loop.

walkthroughs.body_html: map transforms; filter selects; fold (reduce) collapses. Chained together they replace many loops: [1,2,3,4].filter(even).map(square).fold(+,0).
Functional languages often replace loops with recursion. Every recursive function needs a base case and a recursive case that makes progress toward it.
A tail call is the last thing a function does. Compilers can reuse the current stack frame, turning the recursion into a loop and avoiding stack overflow.

options: A base case and a recursive case
